content: Ketotifen is an antihistamine that has been approved by the FDA for the prevention of allergic conjunctivitis. It is administered as an eye drop. The recommended dosage for adults is one drop in the affected eye(s) twice daily, with a dosing interval of 8 to 12 hours, and it should not be used more than twice per day. For children aged 3 years and older, the same dosage applies. For children under 3 years of age, a healthcare provider should be consulted before use. Ketotifen should not be used if you are allergic to any of its ingredients, if the solution changes color or becomes cloudy, or to treat irritation caused by contact lenses. When using this product, contact lenses should be removed prior to application and should not be reinserted for at least 10 minutes after use. To avoid contamination, the tip of the container should not touch any surface, and the cap should be replaced after each use. If you experience eye pain, changes in vision, redness of the eyes, or itching that worsens or persists for more than 72 hours, you should stop using the product and consult a doctor. Keep this medication out of the reach of children. If swallowed, seek medical assistance or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Ketotifen is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA, meaning there is insufficient data to determine its safety during pregnancy. There is no specific guidance on its use during labor and delivery, in nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Additionally, there is no specific guidance on its use in relation to gender, race, or immunocompromised patients. The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of Ketotifen are not well-documented in the drug label. There is also limited information regarding its clinical trial experience, postmarketing experience, drug interactions, and monitoring requirements. If an overdose is suspected, contact the National Poison Help hotline immediately. Ketotifen is supplied for ophthalmic use and should be stored at a temperature of 20° to 25°C (68° to 77°F). The interaction between Ketotifen and alcohol has not been established, so it is advisable to consult a healthcare provider regarding alcohol consumption while using this medication. Ketotifen is marketed under various brand names, including Zaditor, Alaway, Claritin Eye, and Zyrtec Itchy Eye.
